text: {"frames":["\"Follow me, quick, the blue light is moving!\" Lot calls from the barge, and the lantern swings out over the Tower canal. The barge slips off by itself, past the old mill wheel. On the plan under the lantern, the first stretch is {a} cells and the second stretch is {b} cells. The third stretch is {c|cell|cells|cells}, and every cell is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the whole route the blue light has taken you on?","The brass key to the attic has gone from the hook, and the market woman swears she never sold it. She sells keys here to doors that do not exist yet, and she says this one belongs to a door at the far end of the Tower. The plan shows a route with {a} cells along the quay, {b} cells along the dyke, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more up to the attic. Each cell is {d} m on the ground. How many metres long is the route you must walk to reach the door the key belongs to?","You crouch and pull the cupboard away from the wall. Behind it stands a door as tall as a cat, with a keyhole the size of a button. A paper pinned to the door shows a route with {a} cells, then {b} cells, then {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell is {d} m on the ground, and the little door will open only for the right distance. How many metres long is the route on the paper?","A far-off fiddle is playing somewhere under the cheese cellar floor. The cheese makers stop stirring the curds and tilt their heads to listen. The music comes along a route on the cellar plan, which has {a} cells in the first part, {b} cells in the second and {c|cell|cells|cells} in the last. Each cell is {d} m on the ground, and the music grows louder at every step. How many metres long is the route the music has travelled through the cellar?","The hoist beam above the attic door is swinging, although there is no wind. Up in the gable a row of windows lights up one after another, and nobody is inside. Under the gable, a note on the plan shows a route with {a} cells, then {b} cells, and {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell is {d} m on the ground, and the beam will stop swinging only when the walk is measured. How many metres long is the route the swinging beam has marked out?"]}
